en: The Philippines consists of 7,641 islands, correcting the long-held misconception that it only has 7,107 islands.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, not the much shorter Pasig River.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, whereas Mount Pulag is only the third highest.
Taal Volcano is the most active volcano in the Philippines, not Mayon Volcano.
Lake Lanao is the deepest lake in the Philippines, while Laguna de Bay is merely the largest.
Davao City is the largest city in the Philippines by land area, not the capital Manila.
The equator does not cross the Philippines; the entire country is located north of it.
Palawan is geographically and administratively part of the Luzon island group, not the Visayas.
The Cordillera Administrative Region is a region composed of six provinces, not a single province.
Contrary to popular belief, Mindanao lies outside the main typhoon belt and rarely experiences direct typhoon strikes.
The Philippine Sea borders the eastern side of the archipelago, whereas the West Philippine Sea borders its western side.
The endangered tamaraw is found exclusively on the island of Mindoro, not across the entire Philippine archipelago.
